Read about trust and access

Planning your support

Open the topics that matter to your team. These details explain how to prepare the work, review results and handle changes.

A Shopify virtual assistant prepares a bundle launch

In this fictional example, a retailer plans to launch a two-product bundle in its store and one marketplace.

The warehouse count changed after a supplier delay, the two channels display variants differently, and one return is still open. E-commerce operations support connects catalogue readiness, fulfilment and customer messages before the owner confirms the release.

  1. 01

    Match listings to the master catalogue

    For product listing management, check the bundle SKU and components against the approved product file. Verify channel-specific titles, descriptions, images, variants and stock fields. Capture a preview and record any difference that needs a decision about pricing, product claims or an asset before publishing.

  2. 02

    Check stock and order commitments

    A Shopify virtual assistant can compare the storefront, marketplace and warehouse records at the same cutoff. Identify stock reserved for orders or another channel, and flag an unconfirmed supplier date. Check the approved delivery promise and route any stock or launch change to the store owner.

  3. 03

    Release the approved batch and watch exceptions

    Record which listings or promotions were approved and check them after publication. E-commerce operations support can monitor the order and returns queue, confirm that handoffs use the correct SKU and channel, and report any discrepancy alongside the current customer or fulfilment action.

When a task needs your decision

Record the source, what you checked and who can decide. Keep blocked work visible until the next action changes.

Stock counts differ across channels

Link the channel and warehouse records and note the time of each update. A Shopify virtual assistant can show affected SKUs, open orders and the discrepancy without changing the source counts. The inventory owner decides whether to adjust stock or hold a launch.

The product page does not match approval

Check the approved version, SKU and live listing before correcting anything. Product listing management can prepare the proposed correction and identify other channels that use the same asset or field. The owner approves changes to a claim, price or publication status.

A return crosses a policy boundary

Record the order, product, reason and dates and check the approved policy. E-commerce operations support can prepare the response and route the refund or replacement decision with the relevant history. Track the customer’s next update even if the decision is still pending.

Define the inputs for product listing management

Product listing management rules

Share the master product record, channel templates, approved images and who can change each field. Give examples for a single item, variant and bundle. Decide when a change should be drafted, when the store owner can approve a batch and how to record the live page.

Access for a Shopify virtual assistant

Name the storefronts, seller dashboards, help desk, inventory system and fulfilment partner in scope. Set the access needed for reading orders, preparing updates and sending routine replies. Share policies for delays, returns, replacements and billing questions, and identify where exceptions go.

Order and stock reporting rhythm

E-commerce operations support needs a shared cutoff for stock, order status and supplier dates. Decide how to track shipped, delayed, cancelled and returned orders and who checks changes affecting inventory. Use one normal order and one exception to test the handoff.

Review e-commerce operations support

Sample a published listing

Compare the live page with the approved product source. Check variant selection, key details and links on the devices or marketplaces you agreed to review. Product listing management should leave the approval and release date alongside any remaining exceptions.

Check one delayed order and one return

A Shopify virtual assistant can show the source order, latest tracking, current case status and what the customer was told. Look for stale estimates, duplicate messages or cases that appear closed before the responsible owner has acted.

Review the store report and payout handoff

Use e-commerce operations support to compare reported order volume, refunds, stock exceptions and outstanding supplier items with the source systems. Check that the payout and fee files cover the right period before sending them to bookkeeping.

Make the next step clear

Catalogue and launch

Record affected SKUs, approved version, channel, preview and live link. Verify that each published listing reflects the agreed update.

Orders and customer promises

Keep current tracking, promised update and next owner with the case. Continue the conversation with the current delivery information.

Inventory and suppliers

Save counts at the agreed cutoff, discrepancies and supplier follow-up. Resolve open stock questions before a reorder or launch decision.

Returns and payouts

Link the approval, refund status and export period used for bookkeeping. Continue policy and reconciliation review from the recorded state.

Set a weekly rhythm for e-commerce operations support

Normal store operations

Agree when the Shopify virtual assistant checks orders, tickets and inventory, and when the store owner reviews exceptions. Keep a weekly catalogue window for low-risk edits and identify which customer promises cannot wait until that review.

Promotions and product launches

Plan product listing management around confirmed assets, stock, discount rules and delivery promises. Review the preview and inventory before the release window. Arrange coverage for customer enquiries, unconfirmed shipments and changes to approved promotional copy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which stores can you support?

We scope e-commerce operations support around your Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce or other marketplace workflow and the permissions each queue needs.

Can product listing management include publishing?

E-commerce operations support can prepare and check approved product data, descriptions, assets and variants. Agree which updates the assistant can publish after review.

Can you handle returns and customer enquiries?

We can answer approved questions and process routine steps within your rules. Exceptions go to the authorised store owner.

Can you monitor inventory or suppliers?

We can compare records, flag low stock, maintain a vendor follow-up queue and report discrepancies before anyone changes stock or places an order.

Can you help with store accounting?

We can organise orders, payout exports, fees and returns for bookkeeping review. See our accounting and bookkeeping scope for reconciliations.

How do we prepare for a promotion?

Share the dates, approved listings, expected volumes, delivery policies and escalation owners before the launch.
